validation_note: Ten official or public institutional case studies. Analogies are lessons, not diagnoses for Olszówka/Gardeja.

cases.name: Laguna de Aculeo
cases.observed_pattern: NASA reports that the lake dried in 2018 after years of drought and increasing local water use, then partially refilled after exceptional winter rainfall in 2023.
cases.management_lesson: Separate climate-driven recharge from local withdrawals by comparing rainfall, water use and lake-area response through time.

provenance.title: Water Returns to Laguna de Aculeo
provenance.supports: The lake dried in 2018; drought and increasing community/agricultural water use likely contributed, and heavy 2023 rainfall produced partial refill.

cases.name: Mar Menor
cases.observed_pattern: The European Commission describes severe pollution from sewage, agricultural runoff and mining discharges; algal blooms turned the lagoon green and destroyed most seabed vegetation.
cases.management_lesson: A lagoon can retain water while ecological function collapses, so water quantity must be paired with nutrient and oxygen indicators.

provenance.title: Polluted water — Mar Menor
provenance.supports: Mar Menor was severely polluted by sewage, agricultural runoff and mining discharge; algal blooms destroyed 85% of seabed vegetation.

cases.name: Lake Turkana
cases.observed_pattern: UNESCO reports that Lake Turkana receives almost 90% of its inflow from the Omo River and that Gibe III disrupted seasonal flow patterns, with concern over water levels, sediments and salinity.
cases.management_lesson: For downstream lakes, track not only annual inflow volume but also seasonal pulses and sediment delivery from the dominant tributary.

provenance.title: Decision 35 COM 7B.3 — Lake Turkana National Parks
provenance.supports: The Omo supplies almost 90% of Lake Turkana inflow; the Gibe III project was assessed as likely to alter water levels, seasonal flooding, sediment delivery and salinity.

cases.name: Azraq Oasis
cases.observed_pattern: Jordan's UNESCO submission states that water extraction became so great that no surface water remained by 1993 and ecological value was nearly destroyed; restoration began in 1994 and recovered part of the wetland.
cases.management_lesson: Where a wetland is groundwater-fed, surface-water imagery must be interpreted together with pumping and groundwater-level data.

provenance.publisher: UNESCO World Heritage Centre / Jordan Ministry of Environment submission
provenance.title: Azraq
provenance.supports: Excessive water extraction left no surface water by 1993; a rescue effort starting in 1994 restored a significant portion of the wetland.

cases.name: Lake Wuliangsuhai
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank project combined wetlands for pollutant reduction, canals to improve circulation and non-point source controls to reduce nutrient discharge entering the lake.
cases.management_lesson: When poor water quality and weak circulation coexist, source control and hydraulic circulation may need to be managed together.

provenance.title: World Bank Support China to Conserve Cultural Heritage, Improve Water Environment and Expand Railway Network
provenance.supports: The Wuliangsuhai intervention used wetlands, circulation canals and fertilizer/non-point controls to reduce pollution entering the lake.

cases.name: Lake Maracaibo
cases.observed_pattern: NASA satellite observations show oil slicks, sediment and persistent green algal blooms in a nutrient-overloaded estuarine lake affected by oil infrastructure and wastewater/agricultural inputs.
cases.management_lesson: Satellite color anomalies should be classified by likely source—oil, sediment or algae—before inferring a single water-quality cause.

provenance.title: Troubled Waters
provenance.supports: Satellite imagery documents oil slicks, algal blooms, sediment and chronic nutrient overloading in Lake Maracaibo.

cases.name: Lake Powell
cases.observed_pattern: In 2026 the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation reported severe basin drought, very low forecast inflow to Lake Powell and coordinated upstream reservoir releases to reduce risk of falling below critical elevations.
cases.management_lesson: Reservoir management requires a basin-wide water budget: snowpack, inflow, storage and releases must be interpreted together rather than from shoreline position alone.

provenance.title: Drought Response Operations Agreement
provenance.supports: Worsening hydrologic conditions and low reservoir levels led to planned additional upstream releases to support Lake Powell.

cases.name: Xochimilco
cases.observed_pattern: UNESCO describes Xochimilco as a residual lacustrine and canal landscape and identifies regeneration of spring and canal water, chinampa recovery and adjacent water-body land as priority management actions.
cases.management_lesson: In highly modified wetlands, preserve the network of small channels and recharge sources because connectivity can be more important than one open-water polygon.

provenance.title: Historic Centre of Mexico City and Xochimilco
provenance.supports: Xochimilco retains a canal-lake landscape; management priorities include regeneration of spring/canal water and recovery of chinampas and adjacent water bodies.

cases.name: Lake Koroneia
cases.observed_pattern: EU sources document severe pressure on groundwater around Lake Koroneia, declining groundwater availability and lake volume, while an EU Court case found inadequate measures against deterioration and pollution.
cases.management_lesson: Link irrigation demand, groundwater levels, lake volume and wastewater performance in one accounting system; treating them separately can hide the dominant pressure.

provenance.title: Smart water management system to improve crop yield while using less water
provenance.supports: Groundwater near Lake Koroneia is under significant pressure and declining availability is associated with reduced lake volume.

provenance.publisher: Court of Justice of the European Union
provenance.title: C-517/11 Commission v Greece
provenance.supports: The judgment concerns deterioration and pollution of Lake Koroneia and inadequacy of measures including urban wastewater treatment.

cases.name: Gialova Lagoon
cases.observed_pattern: EU CAP research reports that summer losses are dominated by evaporation and that future salinity can worsen unless freshwater inflow is improved by restoring hydrological connectivity with upstream freshwater stores.
cases.management_lesson: A waterbody can degrade because the pathway from upstream storage is broken even when water still exists nearby; map elevation, flow paths and seasonal water balance together.

provenance.title: The hydrology of Gialova Lagoon wetland and restoration needs
provenance.supports: Freshwater inflow and evaporation dominate the lagoon water balance; restoring hydrological connectivity to upstream freshwater stores is identified as a restoration need.
